**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The NONCOMPETE rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position — the agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on AP.

What I checked:
- **Full-text scans** for `compet`, `exclusive`, `restrict`, `shall not`, `may not`, `agrees not to`, `refrain`, and `solicit` across the document body.
- The `shall not` hits are all either Kubient's IP non-infringement warranties (p0033), AP's advertising-content standards (p0041, e.g. no guns/tobacco creative — a content standard, not a competitive restraint), indemnity notice mechanics (p0054), or assignment consent (p0072). None restrict AP's business.
- **Section 1 (p0001)** runs affirmatively in our favour: *"Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties."*
- **Section 2 (p0002)** grants AP a **non-exclusive** license; the "for the purpose of serving Inventory at Target Demand" language is a license-scope limit on AP's use of Kubient's own platform, not a covenant restricting AP's outside activities — correctly not treated as a field-of-use restriction under this rule.

Consistent with the direction guidance, the exclusivity disclaimer benefits our party and was not flagged.
